approach: Add `check_root_cause_diagnosis(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and register it as one `step!` line in `refusing_check` right after `check_code_survey`. It applies when the reading has a capability, no question, class `code` or `tests`, at least one behavior criterion, and the request's trimmed non-bullet lines hold a repair word (fix, fixes, fixing, bug, bugs, regression, or the phrase 'still shows'). It then requires (a) a root-cause criterion that says 'root cause', says where the wrong output enters or why it is not excluded, and names a concrete location (a backticked code span, a crates/ path, or any repo-path token from `path_tokens` whose last segment has a file extension, such as xtask/src/site.rs in plain text), and (b) a behavior criterion that names a test and says it fails on the base tree or without the change. A criterion that equals one of the request's own bullets never counts, so the copied stock bullets are refused. Add `ROOT_CAUSE_GUIDE` and a seventh `READING_RULES` line in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, composed beside `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`. Add unit tests, corpus cases, a CHANGELOG Fixed entry and a short docs/architecture.md paragraph. The gate reads only the reading and request, never the repository. Prompt files, records, xtask and the decisions page are untouched. The 8% share is declared in criterion 4 of the reading (which the replay hold parses) and mirrored in the doc comment and CHANGELOG, labelled an estimate there.

decisions.choice: Fix it at the reading gate with a new `check_*` step in `refusing_check`, not in the decisions page code.
decisions.reason: Both rejected jobs (20261103-201526-t4qv, 20261103-231808-3gkq) moved a filter because the accepted reading never required a diagnosis or a test that fails on the base. The gate is where that reading was accepted. `refusing_check` is the single entry point and refusal_corpus.rs enforces one refusing case per step.

rejected.why: That is one instance; out of scope and the candidates are dropped.
The mechanism default requires a refusal, not prose alone.

decisions.choice: Detect a bug-fix job from the request's prose only. Trim each line (as `request_text_acceptance` does at reading.rs:2402), keep lines where `is_bullet` (reading.rs:2390) is false, lowercase, replace `_` with `x`, and match with `has_phrase` (reading.rs:3366). Triggers, held in one const: fix, fixes, fixing, bug, bugs, regression, and the phrase 'still shows'. 'fixed', 'wrong', 'broken', 'already', 'fails' and 'failing' are NOT triggers.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 1 and 4. 'fixed' is ordinary in feature prose (a 'fixed token budget'), and 'refuse a config with a wrong value' or 'report broken links' are checker features, so those words would cause false refusals. A repair request says fix, bug, regression or 'still shows'. The example request 'The page lists proposals that were already decided; fix it' is still caught by 'fix'. Trimming before `is_bullet` makes an indented bullet count as a bullet, so its 'fails when ...' never triggers. Whole-word matching leaves 'prefix', 'fixture' and `fix_x` alone. A continuation line of a wrapped bullet counts as prose; the doc comment notes this limit.

rejected.option: Keep fixed, wrong and broken as triggers
Count wrong/broken only next to a symptom marker such as 'is wrong'
rejected.why: 'fails when the value is wrong' is still ordinary prose, and the repair words already cover real bug requests; the extra phrases add false-positive risk for little gain.

rejected.option: Match the whole request text including bullets
rejected.why: Feature bullets with 'fails when' would be refused.
Changes the closed class list and config; the reader could pick another class and bypass it.

decisions.choice: The root-cause criterion must (1) contain 'root cause' or 'root-cause', (2) contain a locator stem (where, enter, originat, why, exclud, because), (3) name a concrete location: a backticked code span, `names_crates_path` (reading.rs:3454), or any token from `path_tokens` (reading.rs:3035) whose last segment holds a '.', and (4) not equal any request bullet after `normalised` (reading.rs:3906) with the marker removed. The test criterion must be kind Behavior, contain 'test', contain fail/fails/failing as a whole word, contain a base phrase ('base tree', 'base commit', 'on the base', 'without the change', 'without the fix', 'before the change'), name a test (a backticked span, a crates/ path or 'cargo test'), and not equal a request bullet.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2: the motivating faults were in xtask/src/decisions.rs and xtask/src/site.rs, so a plain-text xtask path must count. `path_tokens` already finds repo paths without backticks and skips URLs, absolute paths and globs. Requiring a '.' in the last segment keeps 'and/or' from counting as a location. The stock bullets (refusal_corpus.rs:227-228) have no location and equal a request bullet, so copying them fails twice over. Whether the test uses real approved and rejected data cannot be decided from text; the guide asks for it and the doc comment marks it prose-only.

rejected.option: Accept only crates/ paths or backticked spans
rejected.why: Refuses the xtask diagnoses that motivated the job (finding 2).

rejected.option: Accept any criterion with 'root cause' plus a locator word

rejected.why: A template refuses good free-text readings.

rejected.option: Mechanically require real recorded data in the test criterion
rejected.why: Not decidable from text without false refusals.

decisions.choice: Put guidance in a new `ROOT_CAUSE_GUIDE` constant plus a seventh `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs, and raise the section-size bound in the brief test. The guide tells the reader to write, in its own words and not the request's bullets, a root-cause criterion naming the file, function or data source where the wrong items enter and why they are not excluded, and a behavior criterion naming a test built from real recorded data of both kinds (approved and rejected) that fails on the base tree and passes with the change.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 asks for a constant composed beside `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`. Every reading check has a rule line (briefs.rs test near 3965), so a new check without one would drift. The reader prompt set (1997 of 2000) and verifier set (1298 of 1300) have no headroom, and the briefs sit outside those sets (docs/system-facts.md).

rejected.why: No token headroom; out of scope.
The criterion asks for a separate constant.

decisions.choice: Declare the share in three places with different jobs. The check's doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry repeat the exact phrase for strangers, each followed by a separate sentence: 'This share is an estimate; the snapshot has no records, so no replay was run when it was written.'
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3: the doc comment and CHANGELOG do not feed the replay hold; they record intent. The unit test applies `replay_declaration` to the reading's criterion 4 text, where '%' is followed by ' of newly refused' as `declared_percent` (reading.rs:3917) requires, and asserts `share == Some(8)`. The estimate caveat stays a separate sentence so the parse is unchanged.

rejected.why: The replay would hold the job at 10% with no recorded intent.

risks.risk: A feature request uses 'fix' or 'bug' as an ordinary word in its prose and is refused.
risks.mitigation: The triggers are narrow (fix, fixes, fixing, bug, bugs, regression, 'still shows'); 'fixed', 'wrong' and 'broken' are not triggers. The check applies only to class code or tests with a capability, no question and a behavior criterion, and matches trimmed non-bullet prose only. The refusal text names the two criteria to add with an example, and `read_for` re-reads once with the refusal as a correction. Corpus and unit Accept cases cover 'a fixed list', 'reports broken links' and 'wrong value'. The trigger list lives in one const, so replay can narrow it.

risks.risk: A criterion that names a path and says 'root cause' passes without a real diagnosis, or states the base-failing test in the negative.
risks.mitigation: The concrete-location and not-a-request-bullet rules remove the copied-boilerplate path. The guide, rule line and error text give the wording and an example. Whether the test uses real approved and rejected data is prose-only, and the doc comment says so.

risks.risk: The location rule accepts a non-location path-like token such as 'and/or'.
risks.mitigation: A `path_tokens` token counts only when its last segment holds a '.', or when it is a crates/ path or a backticked span. A unit test covers 'and/or' alone, which is refused.

risks.risk: The declared 8% is an unmeasured estimate; the real share could exceed it plus the margin and hold the replay.
risks.mitigation: Labelled an estimate in the doc comment and CHANGELOG. Detection is limited to prose and to repair words, which narrows the set. The producer or verifier can shorten the trigger const if the replay holds.

risks.risk: A wrapped bullet's continuation line is read as prose and could carry a repair word.
risks.mitigation: Accepted and noted in the doc comment; the same line shape already limits `request_text_acceptance`.

risks.risk: A new corpus case is refused by an earlier check, so the new check never refuses in the corpus.
risks.mitigation: Cases start from `base_reading`, change class, criterion kinds, assumption and deliverable only, use a `Code survey:` assumption naming a crates/ path present in `repo_files()`, and avoid report/summary wording and job ids. The producer runs the corpus test and reshapes the case, not the check order.

risks.risk: The briefs.rs rule-count test and the `section.len() < 2400` bound fail after a seventh rule and a second guide.
risks.mitigation: Update both in the same change; the producer measures the new section length and sets the bound just above it, with a comment.

risks.risk: This job's own retry is refused by its own gate.
risks.mitigation: Unit test `root_cause_diagnosis_accepts_this_jobs_own_reading` asserts the job's reading shape is accepted.

demonstrations.method: New unit tests in `mod tests` of crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs. Test A (`root_cause_diagnosis_refuses_a_symptom_only_reading`): start from `code_reading(&[SURVEY], &[MODIFY_READING])`, set criteria to one behavior criterion that only describes page content ('Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: the page shows only undecided proposals'), with request 'The page lists proposals that were already decided; fix it.' Call `check_root_cause_diagnosis`, `refusing_check` and `check_reading_acceptance`. Assert the first refusing step is `check_root_cause_diagnosis` and the message names both the missing root-cause criterion and the missing criterion that a test fails on the base tree. Test B (`root_cause_diagnosis_accepts_both_criteria`): add 'The root cause is named: decided proposals enter the page from the unfiltered list built in `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs` and the filter does not exclude them' and a behavior criterion 'The named test `decided_proposals_are_not_listed`, built from approved and rejected proposals, fails on the base tree and passes with the change'; assert Ok from both the check and `check_reading_acceptance`. Test B2: the same root-cause criterion with the location written in plain text as xtask/src/site.rs (no backticks) is accepted (finding 2). Test C (`root_cause_diagnosis_refuses_copied_boilerplate`): the request has the stock dash bullets 'The root cause is named in the change description and fixed where it originates' and 'A test fails without the change and passes with it'; the reading's criteria are those bullets verbatim (second as Behavior); assert refusal by the new check. Test D: a root-cause criterion with 'root cause ... where ... originates' but no path or backticked name is refused; a base-failing criterion with no named test is refused; dropping only the base-failing criterion gives a message naming only that part. Test E (`root_cause_diagnosis_accepts_this_jobs_own_reading`): this job's request prose and brief criteria 1 and 4 are accepted.
demonstrations.observes: A is refused with both missing parts named. B, B2 and E are accepted. C and D are refused by `check_root_cause_diagnosis`.
